record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For every non-complete graph G of order n, does the minimum-degree condition δ(G) ≥ n/2 by itself imply that the rainbow connection number rc(G) equals 2?

evidence.quote: In particular, does δ(G)≥n 2 imply that rc(G) = 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple, finite, connected graph on n vertices. An edge-colouring of G (not necessarily proper) is called rainbow-connecting if between every pair of distinct vertices u, v there exists a u–v path whose edges all receive pairwise distinct colours. The rainbow connection number rc(G) is the minimum number of colours needed for such an edge-colouring. Let δ(G) denote the minimum degree of G.

Question: Is it true that for every non-complete connected graph G on n vertices, the condition δ(G) ≥ n/2 alone implies rc(G) = 2?
artifact.status_search_result: Known results show that δ(G) ≥ n/2 + log n implies rc(G) = 2, while there are graphs with δ(G) = n/2 − 1 and diameter 3 (hence rc > 2). The exact threshold at δ(G) = n/2 appears not to have been settled, and the question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow connection and minimum degree
status_evidence.snippet: Minimum degree n/2+log n guarantees rc(G)=2; minimum degree n/2−1 does not.
status_evidence.claim: The known sufficient minimum-degree bound for rc(G)=2 is slightly above n/2, and δ=n/2 case is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: An updated survey on rainbow connections of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on rainbow connection and minimum degree conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists δ(G)≥n/2 ⇒ rc(G)=2 as an open question.
